question: In the PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) cycle, the 'Do' phase should initially be implemented at full programme scale to gather statistically meaningful data before the 'Study' phase can draw valid conclusions.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. PDSA explicitly uses small-scale tests in the 'Do' phase. The clinical pearl in this SDL emphasises this: test small, learn fast, then spread. Large-scale initial implementation is a common and costly mistake.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is actually FALSE. The strength of PDSA lies in the 'small test' principle — changes are first tested on a small scale (one ward, one ANM, one village) to learn quickly and cheaply before full-scale rollout. Full-scale implementation before study defeats the purpose of the cycle.
